body:
Could you please upload an MRP to make this easier for contributors to troubleshoot?

An MRP is a project that is as small as can be while still reproducing the bug you are reporting. We include the MRP in the bug reporting template as including one greatly increases the chance that a contributor will be able to reproduce the bug you reported and be able to fix it.

In this case an MRP is needed for anyone to assist you. MRPs are very important both to reduce the amount of time that volunteers spend debugging, but also, in many cases the process of creating an MRP helps you further narrow down where the bug is. 

In this case your non-working code has a critical logical flaw, in the process of creating an MRP, you should remove such issues from your code so that the volunteer contributors can focus on what may be an engine bug. 

### Flaw in the non-working code
You are removing surfaces based on an incrementing index, but you are popping the surfaces out from the middle (based on that index) and appending them to the back. Accordingly you will end up not touching every surface. 

If you want to pop and insert, you need to pop from the front each iteration instead of from the loop index

I'll see if I can get a MRP tomorrow when I have time, for now is this better?  Because I still get the exact same issue.  My meshes have 1 or 2 surfaces each and it looks correct in that it:
1. MDT creates from surface index 1 (so, surface 2)
2. Commits from MDT, adding surface index 2 to the mesh (so, surface 3)
3. Removes surface index 1, shuffling the new surface from index 2 to index 1
4. Decrements the index down to 0, and repeats there, then done

or am I still misunderstanding the flaw in the logic?  The surfaces do seem to exist after the fact as you can see in my screenshot above, but they're all squished down tiny and going crazy.  The documentation for commit_to_surface (and surface_remove) don't actually specify what they do, but I'm assuming they add on at the end of the array.

```
	for N: MeshInstance3D in world.get_children():
		var mesh = N.get_mesh()
		if mesh is not ArrayMesh:
			continue
		print("Updating ArrayMesh")
		
		for s in range(mesh.get_surface_count() - 1, -1, -1):
                        # for surface count 2 this does index (1, 0)
                        # for surface count 1 this does index (0)
			print("Updating i ", s)
			var mdt = MeshDataTool.new()
			mdt.clear()
			mdt.create_from_surface(mesh, s)
			mdt.commit_to_surface(mesh)
			mesh.surface_remove(s)
```

Here you can see the inside of a room after the above code runs, this seems to happen to every mesh/surface in the scene.  It's become a tiny little buggy mesh (still has roughly the right form, has the door hole and everything)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fb4e75d-9d1b-4b41-9c40-f9e70b4a3c23)
Reminds me of #103475, can you please try setting the format like it does in the workaround for that issue to confirm this is the same issue?

That's interesting, it does seem related.  I've tried the below code instead and it partially works, some of the surfaces appear to be fine while others still have the previous issue where they get messed up

```
	for N: MeshInstance3D in world.get_children():
		var mesh = N.get_mesh()
		if mesh is not ArrayMesh:
			continue
		
		for s in range(mesh.get_surface_count() - 1, -1, -1):
			var format = N.mesh.surface_get_format(s)
			var mdt = MeshDataTool.new()
			mdt.clear()
			mdt.create_from_surface(mesh, s)
			mesh.surface_remove(s)
			mdt.commit_to_surface(mesh, format)
```

Here the mesh you can see is the entire outdoors surface, its accurate but its scaled down to like 2% of its normal size and all messed up still (z fighting and all sorts of artifacts)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1578408d-8c6b-403c-80ad-3b04479bbb3f)

But the floor of the rooms inside the building appears fine, while the walls are still broken.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23bf7749-a000-4ebe-8457-b7b0fc31d4c0)

For clarity, this is what the mesh normally looks like (I've disabled the vertex colors so you can see the shapes/surfaces)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1b1f499-fc0b-4caf-be3b-77748d764242)
